    “Answered as Christopher Reeve (1952-2004) strictly from documented public biography: Cornell and Juilliard; Broadway debut opposite Katharine Hepburn (1976); Superman (1978) and worldwide fame; two children with Gae Exton (Matthew 1979, Alexandra 1983) and years living in London; marriage to Dana Morosini (April 1992) and son Will (June 1992); the equestrian fall at Culpeper, Virginia on 27 May 1995 causing C1-C2 fracture and quadriplegia, spinal fusion surgery, ventilator dependence and long rehabilitation; advocacy, directing and two memoirs afterwards; diaphragm-pacing surgery in 2003; death on 10 October 2004 from cardiac arrest following an infected pressure ulcer and adverse drug reaction. No reading was seen, so Part D reflects that rather than a judgement of any chapters.”
    “Completed strictly as a biographical exercise from the public record: no reading, chart or verdict was viewed, so Part D's questions about a reading (D1-D7) were left unanswered rather than invented. Where the record is genuinely contested - the exact finalisation of the first divorce, the childhood appendectomy, how much credit is 'deserved' - the answer given is the one a careful biographer could defend from published sources, and the notes field records the reasoning.”
    “I would rather be let alone. What is on the record is enough: a poor childhood in Sodermalm, my father gone when I was fourteen, the store and the barbershop, the Dramatic Theatre school, Stiller, and then America. I worked for a studio for sixteen years, I was never married, I had no children, and after 1941 I did not make another picture. I kept my money, my pictures on the wall, and my privacy. Anything beyond that is other people's invention.”
    “Answered strictly from the documented public record: born 1 October 1924 in the Wise Sanitarium at Plains, Georgia (the first US president born in a hospital); Naval Academy 1943-46; married Rosalynn Smith 7 July 1946; four children (John William 1947, James Earl III 1950, Donnel Jeffrey 1952, Amy Lynn 1967); left the Navy in 1953 after his father Earl's death to take over the family peanut land and warehouse; Georgia state senate 1963-67, defeated for governor 1966, born-again turn 1967, Governor 1971-75, President 1977-81, defeated by Reagan November 1980; left office roughly a million dollars in debt from the warehouse and sold the business; founded the Carter Center in 1982 and taught at Emory; Nobel Peace Prize 2002; metastatic melanoma with liver and brain lesions in 2015, falls and brain surgery in 2019, home hospice from February 2023, Rosalynn's death November 2023. Part D was left blank on purpose - no reading was viewed, so there is nothing honest to say about it.”
    “The record of my life is public to a fault, and I put a good deal of it there myself, some of it wrong on purpose. I was born in Hartford on the twelfth of May, 1907 - though for years I gave out my brother Tom's birthday, the eighth of November, because after he died in 1921 I could not stand to have a day of my own. Take the dates from the books, not from what I said at the time. What matters in it: Tom; my father and mother, who were the two best people I knew; Bryn Mawr; Luddy, whom I married in 1928 and used badly; the pictures; Spencer, for twenty-six years, which was not a settled married life and was never going to be; Fenwick, and the water. I did not want children and I did not have them, and I have never once regretted it. I worked, which is the whole of it.”
    “Answered strictly from documented public biography, in the first person as Stevland Hardaway Morris (b. Stevland Hardaway Judkins, Saginaw, Michigan, 13 May 1950). Born roughly six weeks premature; retinopathy of prematurity (retrolental fibroplasia), associated with the oxygen given in the incubator, left me blind in infancy. Third of six children of Lula Mae Hardaway; my father, Calvin Judkins, was largely absent after my mother took the children to Detroit around 1954, and I later took my mother's married name, Morris. Signed to Motown (Tamla) in 1961 at eleven; 'Fingertips, Pt. 2' went to No. 1 in August 1963. Graduated from the Michigan School for the Blind in Lansing, 1969. Married Syreeta Wright in September 1970; divorced 1972. Let the Motown contract lapse at 21 in 1971 and re-signed on my own terms, with creative control and my own publishing (Black Bull). Nearly killed in a car accident near Salisbury, North Carolina, on 6 August 1973 - four days in a coma, permanent loss of the sense of smell. First child, Aisha Morris, born February 1975; nine children in all. Long campaign that made Dr. King's birthday a federal holiday (signed 1983). Mother died 31 May 2006. Kidney transplant in December 2019. Later married Kai Millard Morris (2001, divorced) and Tomeeka Robyn Bracy (2017); moved to Ghana and took Ghanaian citizenship. Section D was left unanswered: it asks about a reading I was not shown, and I did not open the verdicts or readings folders.”
